notes.title: Levain build schedule
notes.markdown:
## Night before
- [x] Feed the starter 1:5:5 at 9 pm
- [ ] Mix the levain: 20 g starter, 100 g flour, 100 g water

## Bake day
The levain peaks around 8 am in a 22 °C kitchen. It's ready when it has doubled, smells sweet-sour and a spoonful floats.

If the kitchen is cold, put the jar in the oven with just the light on. See [[Sourdough troubleshooting log]] for what went wrong last time.

notes.title: Sourdough troubleshooting log
notes.markdown:
## 3 October
Gummy crumb with a few huge holes under the crust. Loaf spread sideways on the stone and never got any oven spring. Verdict: underproofed — the bulk ferment was only four hours at 19 °C.

## 10 October
Gave bulk six hours with coil folds every 45 minutes. Much better rise, open crumb, ear finally showed up.

Next time: tighter final shaping and a longer cold retard in the fridge.

notes.title: Country loaf formula
notes.markdown:
| Ingredient | Grams | Baker's % |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| White flour | 900 | 90 |
| Whole wheat | 100 | 10 |
| Water | 750 | 75 |
| Levain | 200 | 20 |
| Salt | 20 | 2 |

Autolyse 1 hour, add levain and salt, then bulk ferment until the dough has grown by half. Uses the [[Levain build schedule]].

notes.title: Dutch oven baking notes
notes.markdown:
Preheat the pot for 45 minutes at 250 °C. Lid on for 20 minutes to trap steam, lid off for another 20–25 minutes at 230 °C.

Parchment sling makes loading less scary. Score at 30° with a single confident stroke. Ice cube under the parchment adds a bit more blistering.

notes.title: Discard crackers
notes.markdown:
Use up starter discard instead of binning it.

- 200 g discard
- 100 g flour
- 50 g olive oil, salt, rosemary

Roll thin between two sheets of parchment, cut into squares, bake at 180 °C for 25 minutes until crisp. Keeps for a week in a tin.

notes.title: Flour shopping list
notes.markdown:
- [ ] Strong white flour, 5 kg
- [ ] Stone-ground whole wheat, 1 kg
- [x] Rye for the starter
- [ ] Rice flour for dusting the banneton

The mill by the farmers' market sells 10 kg sacks cheaper than the supermarket.

notes.title: IoT VLAN segmentation
notes.markdown:
## Goal
Put the cameras, plugs, TV and the robot vacuum on their own VLAN 30 so a compromised device can't reach the NAS or laptops.

## Firewall rules
1. VLAN 30 → internet: allow
2. VLAN 30 → LAN: drop
3. LAN → VLAN 30: allow (so Home Assistant can still poll devices)

mDNS reflector is needed or the TV disappears from casting. See [[Router and switch inventory]].

notes.title: WireGuard remote access setup
notes.markdown:
WireGuard listens on UDP 51820 on the router. One peer per device; phone and laptop each get their own key pair and a /32 address in 10.8.0.0/24.

- AllowedIPs on the phone: 10.8.0.0/24 and 192.168.1.0/24 (split tunnel)
- Persistent keepalive 25 s for the phone behind carrier NAT

Rotate keys yearly. QR code import works fine on mobile.

notes.title: Router and switch inventory
notes.markdown:
| Device | Role | Firmware |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Router | Gateway, DHCP, firewall | 4.0.21 |
| 24-port switch | Core, PoE for cameras | 7.1.2 |
| Attic AP | Upstairs wifi | 6.6.77 |

Spare patch cables are in the blue bin in the garage.

notes.title: Pi-hole DNS filtering
notes.markdown:
Pi-hole runs in a container on the NAS and hands out as the only resolver via DHCP. Upstream is a local Unbound instance doing recursive resolution.

Allowlisted: the bank's analytics domain (the login page breaks without it) and the TV's firmware update host.

Blocked queries usually sit around 18 % of total traffic.

notes.title: NAS backup rotation
notes.markdown:
- Nightly snapshots kept for 14 days
- Weekly copy to the USB drive, kept for 8 weeks
- Monthly encrypted upload to off-site object storage

Restore test every quarter: pull one random folder back and diff it. The last test on 1 September passed.

notes.title: Reverse proxy and TLS certificates
notes.markdown:
Caddy fronts every service on the server with automatic certificates via the DNS challenge, so nothing needs port 80 open.

Internal names live under a split-horizon domain; external access only goes through the VPN. Renewal logs are in the Caddy container — check them if a certificate ever shows expired.

notes.title: Hokkaido winter packing list
notes.markdown:
- [ ] Merino base layers (top and bottoms)
- [ ] Down jacket and a waterproof shell
- [ ] Insulated boots with good grip — the pavements in Sapporo are sheet ice
- [ ] Hand warmers, buff, thick gloves
- [x] Universal plug adapter

Leave room for snacks from the airport. See [[Japan itinerary draft]].

notes.title: Japan itinerary draft
notes.markdown:
## Week 1
Tokyo for three nights, then the shinkansen north to Hakodate and on to Sapporo for the snow festival.

## Week 2
Otaru day trip, two nights at an onsen ryokan near Noboribetsu, fly home from New Chitose.

Book the ryokan early — February fills up months ahead.

notes.title: Japan rail pass math
notes.markdown:
The JR Pass for 14 days costs more than it used to after the price rise. Point-to-point tickets for our route:

| Leg | Fare (yen) |
| --- | ---: |
| Tokyo → Hakodate | 23,000 |
| Hakodate → Sapporo | 9,000 |
| Sapporo → Noboribetsu (return) | 6,000 |

Total is well under the JR Pass price, so buy individual tickets.

notes.title: Lisbon weekend recommendations
notes.markdown:
- Pastéis de nata from the bakery in Belém, eat them warm
- Tram 28 early in the morning before the crowds
- Sunset at the Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
- Day trip to Sintra; take the train, not a car

Comfortable shoes — the hills and cobblestones are relentless.

notes.title: Travel documents checklist
notes.markdown:
- [ ] Passport valid for at least six months
- [ ] Travel insurance policy number saved offline
- [ ] Copies of bookings in a shared folder
- [ ] Notify the bank about card use abroad

Keep a photo of the passport photo page somewhere other than the phone.

notes.title: Jet lag recovery routine
notes.markdown:
Shift sleep one hour a day for three days before an eastbound flight. On arrival: daylight in the morning, no naps longer than 20 minutes, caffeine only before noon.

Eastbound is always worse than westbound for me — budget a slow first day.

notes.title: Emergency fund and sinking funds
notes.markdown:
## Emergency fund
Target: six months of essential expenses in a high-yield savings account. Currently at 4.5 months.

## Sinking funds
Monthly transfers into labelled buckets so irregular costs are never a shock:
- Vehicle maintenance and tyres
- Annual insurance premiums
- Vet bills
- Holiday gifts

notes.title: Retirement accounts: Roth IRA vs 401(k)
notes.markdown:
Contribute to the 401(k) up to the employer match first. Then max the Roth IRA, since withdrawals in retirement are tax-free and our bracket is likely higher later.

Anything beyond that goes back into the 401(k). Rebalance once a year in January. Related: [[Annual tax prep checklist]].

notes.title: Annual tax prep checklist
notes.markdown:
- [ ] W-2s and 1099s collected
- [ ] Charitable donation receipts
- [ ] HSA contribution statement
- [ ] Last year's return for reference

File by mid-March so the refund lands before the spring travel bookings.

notes.title: Monthly budget review
notes.markdown:
Second Sunday of each month, 30 minutes:
1. Categorise uncategorised transactions
2. Compare spending against the plan per category
3. Move any surplus into the sinking funds

Dining out ran 40 % over plan in September — mostly the conference week.

notes.title: Mortgage refinance comparison
notes.markdown:
| Option | Rate | Closing costs | Break-even |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Stay put | 6.8 % | 0 | — |
| 30-year refi | 6.1 % | 4,200 | 31 months |
| 15-year refi | 5.6 % | 4,800 | 38 months |

We plan to stay at least five years, so the 30-year refi wins on cash flow.

notes.title: Subscription audit
notes.markdown:
Cancelled: the second streaming service, the unused gym app, the premium weather app.

Keeping: password manager, cloud backup, music.

Saves about 38 a month. Set a calendar reminder to repeat this every six months.
